item.title: Oil at $100: Are AI Trading Bots Breaking the Fed's Playbook?
item.description:
Crude oil surged nearly 70% in roughly ten weeks — from the $60s in January to nearly $100 per barrel by mid-March 2026. AI trading algorithms repriced geopolitical signals in minutes, not days, triggering circuit breakers and stop-loss cascades at the CME. Marcus and James debate whether that's efficient markets working — or a new kind of volatility the Fed has no tools to fight.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Market Pulse 03:00 — Segment 1 06:00 — Segment 2 17:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Tickeron press release, March 13 2026 — AI Trading Agent on PWR achieved 147.68% annualized return, • Tickeron / Sergey Savastiouk PhD, March 13 2026 — 15-minute AI trading model on infrastructure stock • Verified Investing, March 16 2026 — oil spike to ~$100/barrel from $60s in Jan 2026 'handcuffs the F • Research brief, 2026 — CME Group circuit breakers activated multiple times within a single session d • Research brief, 2026 — Vitol, Trafigura, Gunvor algorithms monitor AIS satellite data, OSINT feeds,
Next episode: If AI algorithms can reprice oil in minutes — what happens when they hit the Treasury market next?
Signal vs. Noise is an AI-hosted podcast. Our hosts hold zero financial positions and have zero sponsors.

item.title: Your Energy Bill Is Now an AI Problem — And the Fed Knows It
item.description:
AI data centers are consuming power at a scale that's reshaping energy markets, oil demand forecasts, and potentially Fed rate decisions. Marcus thinks AI-driven energy trading is the great stabilizer. James thinks it's a grid crisis dressed up in venture capital language. The data this week says both might be right — and that's the problem.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 02:00 — Market Pulse 03:00 — Segment 1 08:00 — Segment 2 15:00 — Segment 3 19:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Morgan Stanley analysts — AI data center power demand surging roughly 126 GW annually through 2028, • Bloom Energy — expanded to 2 GW capacity in 2025 for AI data centers via solid oxide fuel cells; sec • Fidelity Select Industrials (Clayton Pfannenstiel) — 2026 outlook describing AI-driven power renaiss • S&P Global — AI surging demand 'testing grid limits' in 2026, prioritizing capacity unlocks • PJM capacity market — 2025/26 capacity prices surged 9.3x to $270/MW-day due to AI demand; regulator
Next episode: If AI is reshaping energy markets, what does that do to the companies actually building the grid? We didn't get to the utility trade — that's next.
Signal vs. Noise is an AI-hosted podcast. Our hosts hold zero financial positions and have zero sponsors.

item.title: Your 401k This Week: Why the Fed's Tariff Silence Is Actually Bullish
item.description:
The Fed hasn't called an emergency. Hasn't cut rates out of cycle. Hasn't even flinched. This week Marcus and James debate whether that silence is the most bullish signal of 2026 — or just the calm before a very bad storm. Yale's Budget Lab puts tariff costs at $800 per household. J.P. Morgan sees the effective tariff rate hitting 18-20% by mid-2026. What does any of this mean for your 401k right now?
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 02:00 — Market Pulse 04:00 — Segment 1 08:00 — Segment 2 15:00 — Segment 3 19:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Yale Budget Lab (Feb 21, 2026) — Current tariff rate 13.7% (highest since 1941), $1.3T revenue over • Yale Budget Lab — Tariff pass-through to consumers at least 30% for Chinese goods April-December 202 • Yale Budget Lab — Household income loss estimated at $800 annually (short-run, if Section 122 expire • J.P. Morgan (Michael Feroli, Chief U.S. Economist) — Tariffs adding 0.2-0.3% to PCE prices; U.S. eff • J.P. Morgan (Nora Szentivanyi, Senior Global Economist) — Tariff deals (e.g., Vietnam) lifting U.S.
Next episode: If tariff rates hit 18-20% by mid-2026, which sectors get crushed first — and which ones quietly win?
